messages:
elaine: FYI hitting a flaky failure in the sample app when rotating credentials inside a dev container.
pranav: what flaky failure exactly?
elaine: we rotate creds by writing a new creds file in /home/dev/.redwood/creds.json and exporting REDWOOD_API_KEY. The running Node app doesn't pick up the new key; new outgoing calls do, but in-flight retries use the old token and sometimes loop into 401s.
noah: that sounds similar to other reports but the container FS makes it worse: overlayfs does atomic renames differently, inode+mTime can be unreliable.
pranav: do we read env only at init? I thought Node SDK checked env each request.
elaine: current sdk-js checks env at init and caches. We started caching to avoid calling KMS providers every request.
noah: suggestion: policy = env checked on each request, but cache token for short TTL (default 2s). On 401 retry, force a refresh and re-fetch token. That avoids extra KMS calls while handling rotations.
elaine: +1. Also for file-backed providers use a cheap file-change detector: compare mtime + 8-byte file-hash (sha1 prefix). Overlay/atomic renames tend to preserve strange metadata so hash helps.
pranav: agree. Add opt-out: REDWOOD_CRED_HOTRELOAD=false for deterministic infra tests. Also make a client option credHotReload: boolean to set per-client.
noah: API: add Client.refreshCredentials(force=false) so ops can call it after rotation hooks. And internally, on retry after 401/403 call refreshCredentials(true) before retrying.
elaine: another important invariant: REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID and REDWOOD_ORG_ID must be init-only. If those env values change at runtime we should log an error and throw on next request. Routing should not mutate mid-process.
pranav: good call. Also add a short info log when token source changes (env -> file -> kms) and when a retry triggers a credential refresh. Makes debugging easier for sample-app maintainers.
noah: note for docs: explain file rotation behaviors per OS (macOS, linux overlayfs, windows). Recommend using env export for simple cases, but show rotate script that writes file + exports + calls client.refreshCredentials().
elaine: sample: ```sh
# rotate-demo.sh
echo '{"api_key":"NEW"}' > /home/dev/.redwood/creds.json
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=NEW
# tell long-running test app to reload
curl -sS localhost:4000/-/trigger-reload || true
# or call JS client refresh API
node -e "require('./client').client.refreshCredentials(true)"
```
pranav: mention atomic rename edge: when tools write then mv tmp->creds.json, check both mtime and sha1. Implementation note: don't block request path on expensive hash; do quick mtime check then spawn async hash compute and swap if differs.
noah: will add a lightweight checksum util with buffered reads. For tiny creds file cost is trivial.
elaine: opened GH issue #1760 to track cross-SDK parity and sample app changes. tagging @eng-sdk and @qa.
qa-bot: CI note: adding integration test rotate-inflight.sh -> should assert client recovers and does not loop 401s. Will add to flaky-tests job.
eng-sdk: PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1102 - feat: cred hot-reload + retry refresh + file-checksum detection (CI: pending)
elaine: thanks everyone. I'll validate in the container and paste logs if anything odd.
